flags.detail: The keyed letter C is the best of the four (A, B and D are all outright false), but both option C and the explanation state a 'minimum billable object size' as a universal property of cold/archive object-storage classes, and it is not — it is AWS-specific. Google Cloud Storage's own storage-classes doc lists 'No minimum object size' as a characteristic shared by ALL its classes including Nearline/Coldline/Archive (it has only minimum storage durations of 30/90/365 days). Azure Blob's access-tiers doc likewise defines cool/cold/archive purely by minimum retention (30/90/180 days) with no minimum billable blob size anywhere. Even on AWS the phrase is loose: the 128 KB minimum billable object size applies to S3 Standard-IA, One Zone-IA and Glacier Instant Retrieval, whereas Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive instead charge a fixed 40 KB per-object metadata overhead (8 KB at Standard rates + 32 KB at the Glacier rate) — AWS documents that as 'storage overhead charges', not a minimum object size. The stem names no provider, so a student memorises 'archive classes have a minimum billable object size' as a general rule and it is wrong on two of the three major providers. Fix: either pin the stem to AWS S3, or rewrite the option/explanation so the two mechanisms that ARE universal (minimum storage duration, and a chargeable per-object transition request) carry the answer, with the minimum-object-size point demoted to a provider-specific aside.
flags.suggested: Keep key C. Pin the stem to 'Amazon S3', or reword C to 'Archive classes bill each object for a minimum storage duration and add a fixed per-object storage overhead, and each transition is itself a chargeable request'.

flags.detail: The scenario premise no longer holds on AWS with a default-configured rule. Since September 2024 S3 Lifecycle applies a default behaviour that prevents objects smaller than 128 KB from transitioning to ANY storage class (docs.aws.amazon.com, 'Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle' → Constraints and considerations): 'Amazon S3 applies a default behavior to S3 Lifecycle configurations that prevents objects smaller than 128 KB from being transitioned to any storage class.' Before September 2024 the default did allow sub-128 KB objects through to Glacier Flexible Retrieval and Deep Archive — which is exactly the behaviour this question is written against. So a team that 'adds a lifecycle rule that transitions every object' of 20 KB would, on AWS today, transition nothing at all and see no bill rise; producing the described outcome now requires explicitly overriding the default with an ObjectSizeLessThan/ObjectSizeGreaterThan filter or the x-amz-transition-default-minimum-object-size header. This is the exact 'true in 2019, since changed' failure mode. Fix: state in the stem that the rule carries an explicit object-size filter allowing objects below 128 KB, or set the scenario on a provider with no such guard (GCS Archive, Azure archive tier), where minimum storage duration plus per-object transition operations still produce the cost increase.
flags.suggested: Add to the stem: '...adds a lifecycle rule, with an explicit object-size filter so that even these small objects are included, that transitions every object to the provider's archive storage class 7 days after creation.'
